title: When Does an Aesthetic Become a System?
author: RN Collins
principle: Evidence leads; atmosphere never substitutes for provenance.

narrativeSequence.caption: An aesthetic becomes a system when recurring choices are connected to roles, evidence, tests, handoffs, exceptions, and feedback—so the practice can learn without reducing itself to visual sameness.
The sheet demonstrates a contract-shaped network of design, printing, manufacture, advertising, attribution, and distribution—even when the operative agreements are absent from the image.
narrativeSequence.rights: Free to Use and Reuse / Library of Congress curated set

narrativeSequence.caption: 01 · INPUT — What enters the aesthetic system?. Inventory references, materials, bodies, techniques, constraints, memories, commissions, budgets, deadlines, collaborators, and cultural knowledge. Attach origin, permission, credit, context, and transformation status to every consequential input.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 02 · RULE — How does an input change a decision?. Translate a mood into a testable relation: if the material has this weight, the silhouette permits this movement; if the image uses this distance, the body retains this agency. Preserve exceptions and who may authorize them.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 03 · LOOP — How does the system learn?. Connect sample, fitting, wearer response, production constraint, image review, sales signal, repair evidence, criticism, and archive return. Record which feedback changed the work and which was rejected with reason.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 04 · RIGHTS — Which outputs or identifiers may be protected?. Map exact works, marks, registrations, contracts, designs, files, and confidential methods separately. Do not convert system documentation into a claim that the overall aesthetic is automatically copyrighted or registrable.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
